title: Easy to panic, hard to master: a co-op spaceship game for friend groups who like a challenge (and to show off their skills)
author: Pere-Castor-
selftext:
Hi everyone!

Full disclosure, I don't know how to code but I love video games and creating.

This is the result of 3 months of Claude writing every single piece of code, art and sound and me being the head of design making every decision and testing+approving every change.

The idea is simple, as I grew older, I found myself not having the time to play solo games, and to be honest, also not enjoying them the way I use to. When I want to play, it's to spend time with my friends, as I'm living abroad on a different time zone. So I want to make the best out of this quality time. It has to be quick, fun and chaotic (with a touch of trash-talking) and to require a bit of skill (to show off), all of that while being challenging, to feel rewarding.

I've tried to encapsulate all of that into one, to create memories.

The result is **Survive in Spaceshit: The Reversal**, a 1–6 player online co-op game. 

The universe is collapsing behind you, and your crew has to keep a falling-apart spaceship alive while you outrun the end of everything.

**What the game is:**

* Think *Overcooked* meets *FTL - (for the fun and chaotic part)*
* 50+ hands-on minigames (think Among Us, but with popular inspired games) across the ship’s stations (logic, mazes, rhythm, reflex, precision, memory, communication etc.) - (*to show off your skills*)
* Keeping the ship alive when everything breaks: fires, breaches, floods, faults, and crewmates who forgot to eat or sleep
* Hard to master. It’s chaos at first, games don't last long. But skilled, coordinated crews go much further.

![gif](fhshayijvxvh1)

**How I built it:**

* The whole game is **one single HTML5 file** with no external libraries, drawn on a 2D canvas, and wrapped in Electron for Steam.
* Just over 500 numbered builds over 3 months. Each session I give feedback like a designer, and Claude patches the file, as simple as that.
* The art and sound is drawn in code too: every ship part, music and effect is canvas drawing

**What I learned:**

* **Versioning saves you.** When a change went wrong, having every build numbered meant we could always go back.
* **Testing matters more than writing.** Automated playthroughs caught bugs I’d never have found alone.
* **The design is still yours.** AI can build fast, but deciding what’s fun, what to cut, and what the game *feels* like is still the human job.

**What's left** ***(that AI cannot do)*****:**

* Play testing with friends to find the right balance in difficulty.
* Test more online/multiplayer mode to find all possible bugs and lags.
* Make the game as fun as possible.
* Find a community that may enjoy this game.

I’d love your feedback (on anything, really), and I’m happy to answer any questions about the workflow!

I already have the steam page up if you wanna go see more: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5365370/Survive\_in\_Spaceshit\_\_THE\_REVERSAL/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5365370/Survive_in_Spaceshit__THE_REVERSAL/)
